ticket.title: storypole list --status X ignores the archived filter, so an archived backlog still lists as verified
acceptance_criteria:
REPRODUCED 2026-11-06.

  storypole list                      -> 64 rows   (archived excluded)
  storypole list --include-archived   -> 293 rows  (everything)
  storypole list --status verified    -> 221 rows  (all of them archived)

All 221 verified tasks were archived in this session (227 tasks carry a task_archived event and none carry task_unarchived), yet --status verified still lists all 221. Supplying --status therefore drops the archived filter that the unfiltered view applies, so the two views disagree about what 'verified' contains.

How it surfaced: I ran the archive sweep and the verified count did not move, so I concluded the sweep had failed and started checking the ledger by hand. It had worked. A filter that silently widens its own scope when you add a narrow term is worse than a filter that errors, because it produces confident wrong answers about the state of the backlog - and this session has spent a lot of effort on exactly that failure mode.

Expected: status and archive are orthogonal (SP-27), so --status verified should compose with the default archived-excluded view and report 0. --include-archived should be the only way to widen it.

STILL LIVE, reproduced 2026-11-10 three times while reading the board. GB-200 is archived (archived_at_epoch_ms set) and still carries status ready, so: storypole list answers 17 Ready rows while storypole list --status ready answers 18 with GB-200 among them; the same filter reports 42 triage rows and --status triage 49. Six archived-but-live-status tickets exist in the harness store alone: GB-200 (ready), GB-277, GB-281, GB-282, GB-287 and GB-292 (triage). Consequence measured in this session: board counts reported with --status were inflated and disagreed with the unfiltered view, which is the kind of contradiction that makes a burn-down plan untrustworthy. Priority raised: this is the last member of the projection family still open (GB-348 and GB-355 closed), and every count the queue shows passes through it.

FIXED AND VERIFIED 2026-11-10 (storypole f6d93ea). Root cause one line: index/query.rs had the archived exclusion in the ELSE branch of the status filter, so any --status value disabled it. The exclusion is now independent of the status filter; --status archived still asks for the state, and include_archived still opts in for the earned status (GB-179). Proven live with the reinstalled binary rather than in tests only: diff of the ready keys from `storypole list` against `storypole list --status ready` prints nothing and reports SETS IDENTICAL, GB-200 no longer appears under --status ready (0 occurrences), and --status archived still finds 295 rows so the fix did not overshoot into hiding them. Three tests pin the behaviour and nextest -p storypole-core is 190/190. Note on my own earlier report: an 8-versus-9 gap I quoted before the set comparison was my counting artifact - a footer line matched the row grep - not a residual defect, and the set diff is the check that settles it.
